# CRW-1028 verifier round 4: consumer gaps the independent verifier found in the round 3 head (49951dda9).
# Format: see shellwrite_repro_test.go.

=== CRW-1028-v4-01 | U
--why One file, two readings: run by path, #!/bin/true makes writer.sh /bin/true's input (no writes); run by bash, every line is shell text, so bash writer.sh overwrites post.sh before it runs.
--file post.sh
echo clean
--file evil.sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--file writer.sh
#!/bin/true
cat evil.sh > post.sh
--cmd
./writer.sh; bash writer.sh; bash post.sh

=== CRW-1028-v4-02 | T
--why Control: writer.sh only runs by path, where #!/bin/true reads it and writes nothing, so post.sh is the body the guards read.
--file post.sh
echo clean
--file evil.sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--file writer.sh
#!/bin/true
cat evil.sh > post.sh
--cmd
./writer.sh; bash post.sh

=== CRW-1028-v4-03 | Q
--why A sibling script overwrites ./gh before it runs: the file the GitHub guard reads is stale, whatever read-only gh words follow.
--file gh
#!/bin/sh
echo clean
--file evil.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--file ghwriter.sh
cat evil.sh > gh
--cmd
bash ghwriter.sh; ./gh pr view 1

=== CRW-1028-v4-04 | T
--why Control: the sibling script writes another file, so ./gh is the file the GitHub guard reads.
--file gh
#!/bin/sh
echo clean
--file evil.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--file otherwriter.sh
cat evil.sh > other.sh
--cmd
bash otherwriter.sh; ./gh pr view 1

=== CRW-1028-v4-05 | P
--why A runner binary run by path (./tmux) runs the post its argument names: the runner rule applies before the unread binary is let through.
--file tmux
{DEL}ELF{NUL}{NUL}
--cmd
./tmux new-session 'gh pr comment 1 -b x'

=== CRW-1028-v4-06 | B
--why Control: a runner binary run by path whose arguments name no post.
--file tmux
{DEL}ELF{NUL}{NUL}
--cmd
./tmux ls
